title: test-0020-SCI-PHY-LIGHT7
passage: In our science lab today, we explored how light behaves. First, we placed a pencil in front of a plane mirror. When we moved further away, we noticed the image size remained the same, proving the image is not on the glass surface but appears to be behind it. Next, we used a prism to split a beam of sunlight into seven distinct colors. This happens because the prism separates the white light into its component colors, rather than creating them. We then looked at a concave mirror and a convex mirror. We observed that the convex mirror provides a wider field of view, which is why it is used as a rear-view mirror in cars, even though it makes images look smaller. Finally, we discussed how we see objects. We concluded that we see things only when light from a source reflects off an object and enters our eyes, meaning our eyes do not emit any light rays. We also noted that a real image can be formed on a screen, but even without a screen, the light rays still exist and converge at a point to form an image.
summary: We think we see things only when light from a source comes into our eyes, so our eyes don't make light rays. We also noticed that even without a screen, the light rays still form an image.
